notes:
Three bullets, one of which is the whole quest. Bullet 2 -- 'visit and test the three Hot Springs, under different conditions, to obtain 5 reports' -- is not one step but three places, so it becomes three grouped rungs at (H-7), (H-8) and (G-8), all drawn at once because the springs may be visited in any order and the sub-bullet's 'start at Bivouac #2 and go south' is a suggestion, not an order.

The 'After the walkthrough: Hot Spring Reports' section (its own [1]..[8] numbering) is where the quest actually lives: it pins report 3 to the H-7 spring, report 4 to H-8 and report 5 to G-8, and says reports 1 and 2 come from any spring. Those pinnings are folded into each step's note. Its numbering is also broken -- [3]/[4], [5]/[6] and [7]/[8] are each one report split across two bullets by the renderer -- which is why the source_bullets here cite the walkthrough's [2] rather than that section's.

No evidence anywhere, and that is a real loss rather than laziness: 'Hot spring report 1'..'5' are named on the page but resolve against neither res/items.lua nor res/key_items.lua, so nothing about this quest is observable. They are therefore not recorded as items on the turn-in either -- the page never marks them [KI], so even the kind would be a guess. The whole thing is gated on game-clock windows the addon cannot see (the page is explicit that there is NO weather requirement and that it is purely time), and the page carries the wiki's own 'unverified' / 'Information Needed' markers with several windows left open-ended. Hence medium.

notes:
A delivery round, and the whole thing happens in one zone: 'Southern San d'Oria (S)' is the wiki form and resolves to zone 80, so it is written as the page writes it.

Bullet 1 is not a step -- it is a reassurance that you need not be allied to San d'Oria. Bullet 3 is a step, but a strange one: you must LEAVE and come back, so it is a second conversation with Louxiard rather than a travel rung, with the Retrace tip in the note.

Bullet 4 is one bullet holding eight things: a conversation with Rholont and seven deliveries. The seven share a group and all draw at once. The page does not say 'in any order' outright, but it is a list of recipients read out in a cutscene, and the alternative -- a strict ladder that marks Machionage and then nothing until you happen to walk past him -- is the failure mode groups exist to prevent. Louxiard appears twice on purpose: he is both the giver and one of the seven recipients.

Holding a Plume d'Or is what proves Rholont has handed them out, so it is step 3's evidence at count 1 rather than 7 -- the page never states how many you receive, only how many people want one, and one is enough to know the cutscene has played.

The Previous field reads 'The Fighting Fourth, Snake on the Plains, or Steamed Rams'. That is an OR, and prev is an AND everywhere downstream, so recording all three would block the quest for a player who did exactly what the page asks. prev is left empty and the three are named here instead: under-gating shows the quest a little early, over-gating hides it from people who can actually do it. The Lore wikitable is spoilers, not steps.

notes:
Four bullets, four rungs, and both evidence points are real key items -- the cleanest page in this batch.

The one judgement call is the protocrystal. The walkthrough never mentions clicking anything: bullet 2 only says 'travel to Cape Teriggan (F-5) to enter the Cloister of Gales'. But the header's Description says outright 'Ring the tuning fork of wind upon the protocrystal', and note 6 calls it 'the Protocrystal', so the trade IS on the page and is recorded as a rung. It is named 'Protocrystal' -- exactly what the page calls it -- and NOT 'Wind Protocrystal', which is what the live entity in that zone is called elsewhere in this corpus (Carbuncle Debacle's page spelled it out, so that quest could use it; this one does not). This is the Class Reunion situation repeating, and the page wins over the guess. If a human wants the marker back, 'Wind Protocrystal' is the string to try -- it folds to a key the runtime already carries at zone 201.

Cape Teriggan is not given a rung of its own: the Cloister of Gales is entered from (F-5) and the trade happens inside it, so the route is a note on the trade, matching how Carbuncle Debacle handled the same journey.

Fame 'r / 6' is Rabao, which the resolver folds into the shared rabao_selbina region. The whole Notes section is cooldowns, party rules and a Summoner-only shortcut through another quest -- none of it is a step, and the Mini Fork of Wind route in note 6 is deliberately not modelled because it belongs to Trial-Size Trial by Wind, not here.

ADVERSARY (stage D): quest confidence lowered high -> medium, nothing else touched. The walkthrough never states the quest's central action -- bullet 2 only sends you to Cape Teriggan -- so the trade rung exists only because the header's Description states it; that is an incomplete page, which is the medium criterion. The rung's own object name is also the one thing here that will not draw: the page says 'the protocrystal' and the live entity in Cloister of Gales is 'Wind Protocrystal', so step 2 keeps its position but loses its marker. Renaming it is not this stage's to do. Everything else re-checked and left alone: both key items are granted at the rung that carries them (fork at 1, whisper at 3), neither is in the Reward list, the fork is items on 2 and evidence only on 1, and the Cloister of Gales zone on steps 2 and 3 is right -- the cloister is the zone entered from Cape Teriggan (F-5) and the protocrystal stands inside it.

notes:
This page is written as a reference sheet, not a walkthrough, and reading it as a sequence would be wrong. Bullets 3, 4 and 5 are not three errands: they are three ALTERNATIVES, one per monster type, and a single run of this repeatable quest involves exactly one of them. The page gives it away twice -- bullet 2 says 'you travel to a beastman stronghold and spawn a NM', singular, and the loose line after bullet 5 says 'if solo, the Wamouracampa is recommended', which is only advice if you are choosing.

An OR of three has no representation in the schema, so they are put in one group. That is not literally what a group means, but it produces the behaviour a player wants -- all three draw at once, and you go to whichever one you picked -- whereas a strict ladder would mark Arrapago Reef and refuse to acknowledge the other two. Flagged as or_branch_modelled so this is findable.

The spawn ??? are folded into the fight rungs rather than given their own: the page mentions a ??? only for the Orobon, and only in passing to say you may need a key to reach it. That key is recorded as items with items_partial set, because the Ilrusi Atoll Staging Point route needs none.

Bullets 6 and 7 are two separate conversations with Hishahma -- you must zone in between to hear whether you were right -- so they stay two rungs and one marker. The After the walkthrough note is a real prerequisite beyond the header's 'Previous: Finding Faults': Finding Faults must be done with ALL THREE monster types before this is even offered, which prev cannot express since it is the same quest three times over. Nothing in this quest is observable, so there is no evidence anywhere. Medium for the OR and for how loosely the page is written.

notes:
Short, and almost entirely made of things that are not steps. Bullet 2 is the Moogle's REQUEST, not a second errand, and its sub-bullet is idle dialogue if you talk to him again -- so bullets 1 and 2 are one rung, and the Fruit Seeds he hands over in that cutscene are its evidence.

Bullet 3 is the real work and is three different things stacked into one bullet with its sub-bullets: get a Sunsand, grow a Tropical Cactus, trade it. The Sunsand ??? in Valkurm Dunes (H-9) gets its own rung because it is the only real PLACE in the quest -- but it is optional and it always will be, since the page says outright that buying the cactus off the Auction House skips the whole gardening branch. It is also gated on dusty weather, which the addon cannot see.

The cactus rung is an obtain with no place: you may plant any seed (the Fruit Seeds will do, and a Revival Tree Root matures in an hour), fertilise with a Sunsand and harvest, or simply buy one. items_partial says there is a route items cannot express. No combination guarantees a cactus, so several Sunsands may be needed -- a loop no count can hold.

Bullet 4 is the reward, not a step, and the [KI] Sheep companion it names is a reward besides, so it is not evidence anywhere. It does not resolve against res/key_items.lua either, which costs nothing here. The three prerequisite quests are in both Quest Reqs and Previous and are recorded; their sub-conditions (mount access, level 7 in all Geological Locations, level 7 Monster Rearing) are Mog Garden state that nothing observable reports.

steps.note: no need to zone after finishing the three prerequisite quests. The cutscene hands over the Fruit Seeds and asks you to plant them with a Sunsand as fertiliser -- that request is bullet 2, and it is not a separate errand.
